subject: Banking
title: Silicon Valley Bank: A Modern Run
description: A 60-second lesson on Silicon Valley Bank: A Modern Run.

hook.text: In March 2023, Silicon Valley Bank collapsed in 48 hours.

buildup.text: SVB had invested deposits in long-term bonds. When interest rates rose, those bonds lost billions in value.

discovery.text: Tech startups panicked. Twitter and group chats spread fear faster than any 1930s bank run.

twist.text: The FDIC insured only $250,000 per account. Most SVB depositors held millions.

climax.text: SVB proved that bank runs in the digital age happen in hours, not days. Speed changes everything about banking crises.

punchline.text: $42 billion withdrawn in one day. Modern bank runs happen by app.

quiz.question: What made the SVB bank run unique?
options: Depositors withdrew $42 billion in one day via digital banking

details.summary: Silicon Valley Bank's 2023 collapse was the first major bank run of the social media era, where tweets and group chats accelerated withdrawals to a speed that overwhelmed both the bank's liquidity and regulators' ability to respond.
details.whyItMatters: SVB proved that the traditional bank run has been transformed by technology. A modern run can destroy a bank in hours, raising fundamental questions about whether the existing regulatory framework can protect depositors.
takeaways: Customers withdrew $42 billion in a single day through mobile and online banking
Venture capitalists coordinated withdrawals through social media and group chats
The run happened too fast for the Fed's traditional lending tools to help

faq.question: How was the SVB run different from historical bank runs?
faq.answer: Traditional runs required depositors to physically line up at branches, naturally limiting withdrawal speed. SVB's customers moved billions with phone taps, and social media spread panic faster than any regulator could counteract.

faq.question: Could the SVB-style run happen to other banks?
faq.answer: Any bank with concentrated, largely uninsured deposits and unrealized asset losses is vulnerable. The SVB template of social media-amplified panic driving instant mobile withdrawals could be replicated against similarly exposed institutions.
